scope: released-case evidence-locus augmentation only; no claim, practice-extent, P-level, publication or release-membership mutation

released_case.canonical_name: Iraq/Syria under ISIL, especially Yazidi population from 2014

historical_evidence.title: The ISIL Attack on Sinjar in August 2014 and Subsequent Acts Committed Against the Yazidi Community in Iraq
historical_evidence.independence_note: This is the already accepted source family for both released claim facets. The geometry recovery adds no new independent historical attestation.

locators.relevance: Yazidis were captured across Sinjar, explicitly including Sinjar town; separation by age and gender began the organized slave-trade and enslavement system.
Women, boys and girls were taken to initial holding sites including Sinjar town before onward movement to Ba'aj, Mosul, Tal Afar and other sites.

Women and girls were selected from holding sites and distributed through lottery, sale or gift; use this only to contextualize Sinjar as an upstream holding-stage locus, not as the location of every later sexual-slavery act.

new_locus_entity.notes: Named capture and initial-holding locus in UNITAD's 2014 Sinjar case assessment. This site identity does not define ISIL territorial control, regional practice extent or prevalence.

geometry.resolution_method: Use the modern GeoNames populated-place coordinate for Sinjar/Sinjar town as navigation geometry for the enduring named town. UNITAD explicitly identifies Sinjar town as both a capture location and an initial holding site in the 2014 enslavement system. The modern point is not a practice extent, not an ISIL boundary and not the coordinate of every act described in the case assessment.

locus_links.role_text: UNITAD-documented Yazidi capture and initial-holding locus in Sinjar town
locus_links.notes: UNITAD paras. 193 and 195. Evidence locus for the released enslavement facet; not territorial extent or prevalence.

locus_links.role_text: UNITAD-documented initial-holding stage feeding the later distribution/sale system
locus_links.notes: UNITAD paras. 195–196. Sinjar town is an upstream holding-stage locus in the system; this does not assert that every later sexual-slavery act occurred in Sinjar town.

deferred.reason: UNITAD strongly supports Kocho as a capture site, but modern coordinate references conflict materially. Do not silently normalize competing Kocho/Kuju coordinates in this tranche.
